routing.ruling: Curriculum, not reference. The seven PDFs form one coherent remedial reading program: a diagnostic and introduction, a sequenced 40-lesson teacher guide, controlled reading material, flashcards, two practice games, and a completion checklist. Its value is the teaching method, placement logic, scope and sequence, recurring lesson structure, and per-lesson mastery progression. Those are the five curriculum layers, not the layout and print traits of one standalone worksheet. The curriculum-ingestion rule also treats a coherent multi-file curriculum wave as one analysis rather than fragmenting its companion assets into separate references.
routing.recipeRuling: All eight Layer 4 recipe gaps graduated on reusable Homa-owned surfaces. Reading placement and mastery observation use the phonics-spelling diagnostic recipe only when deterministic code supplies the policy, ordered skills, stops, and result route. Text-only phonics bingo remains the same shuffled-board mechanic as picture bingo. The source-specific flash-card name aliases to the existing subject-neutral flash-card format. Five distinct mechanics received self-contained recipes. No source word list, story, game rule, threshold, page geometry, or visual identity entered the skill package.

name: Stairway to Reading

layer1_philosophy.methodology: Diagnostic-placement, one-to-one, mastery-based systematic phonics remediation
principles: Begin with a two-part diagnostic that tests decoding of unfamiliar words and oral reading level, then start at the first missing skill rather than at a fixed age or grade lesson.
Teach sound-letter correspondences and blending in a strict sequence, and do not advance until the current step can be performed accurately and fluently.
Use immediate, matter-of-fact correction, praise correct responses, and discourage guessing at unfamiliar words.
Build automaticity through daily practice, repetition, repeated reading, and several short, varied activities rather than one long drill.
Keep the intervention adaptive: the diagnostic chooses the entry lesson, lesson mastery chooses when to advance, and identified weak areas receive targeted practice.

layer1_philosophy.assessmentApproach: initial diagnostic placement plus an explicit word-reading mastery check at the end of each lesson
layer1_philosophy.parentRole: one-to-one instructor who prepares materials, models and prompts decoding, corrects errors immediately, varies practice, records completed activities, and decides when mastery is secure

knowledgeBankMatches.note: Both methods are explicit, sequential, phonics-led, and mastery-gated. Stairway is not DISTAR: it is not fully scripted, begins with diagnostic placement, uses segmenting rather than continuous blending as a later recurring routine, and recommends up to an hour daily rather than a fixed 20-minute lesson.

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Stairway to Reading lesson format
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: A 40-lesson remedial reading sequence supported by a placement test, lesson guide, decodable reading material, flashcards, word bingo, Crazy Letters card games, a completion checklist, and progress graphs. Each lesson identifies who needs it, names the skill, rotates short practice activities, and closes with a word-reading mastery check.

layer3_structure.cadence: Daily one-to-one instruction. Frequent, short sessions are preferred to irregular, long sessions, and the guide says the best results come from at least some instruction every day.
layer3_structure.cadenceEvidence: Frequent, short sessions are more effective than irregular, long sessions.

sessionLengthMinutes.evidence: A commitment of approximately one hour a day is recommended, but even 15 minutes of instruction a day can make a big difference.

layer3_structure.weeklyTemplate: No weekday template is prescribed. Start at the lesson selected by the diagnostic. In each daily session, rotate activities in blocks of no more than five or ten minutes, such as flashcards, letter or word manipulation, notebook work, word sorting, sentence reading, dictation, Bingo, Crazy Letters, and a decodable story. End on a successful activity, note what was completed, and continue the same lesson in later sessions until the mastery words are read with ease.
layer3_structure.progressionModel: Linear, diagnostic-entry, mastery progression through 40 lessons. Students may begin at Lessons 1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 12, or 13 according to the diagnostic, but once placed they proceed in sequence and do not advance until the current lesson is fluent.
layer3_structure.reviewRhythm: Every lesson ends with TESTING MASTERY. Segmenting becomes a five-minute opening routine from Lesson 19 onward, prior sound spellings remain in the flashcard deck, and repeated story reading is recommended when accuracy, comprehension, or fluency needs more practice.
layer3_structure.durationRange: The source gives a shortest possible completion time of about six weeks and a longest possible time of a year or more, so a fixed week count would be false.
layer3_structure.durationEvidence: The shortest possi-ble time to complete the program is about six weeks, while the longest possible time is a year or more.

layer5_lessons.notes: All 40 numbered lessons in the lesson guide are decomposed. The companion Reading Material, Flashcards, Crazy Letters, Bingo, and Checklist files are supporting assets referenced by those lessons, not additional lesson units. The lessons prescribe decoding activities and mastery word checks but do not print fixed comprehension questions or literary themes, so questions and themes remain empty instead of being invented. The program is for struggling readers of any age, so unit-level age ranges are omitted.

notes: Stairway to Reading is a coherent seven-file capture totaling 415 pages: introduction and diagnostic, 40-lesson teacher guide, controlled Reading Material, flashcards, two practice games, and a lesson checklist. Its distinctive contribution is diagnostic-entry, one-to-one phonics remediation with a mastery check at every step. The full text sidecar covers every page. One rotated source page was normalized during intake, and the manifest reports no remaining unreadable-page gate finding. On 2026-08-02 all eight Layer 4 recipe gaps graduated: four through explicit aliases to broader recipe owners and four through direct source-named recipes, with flash-cards also receiving its first self-contained generic recipe. All twelve activity types now resolve to shipped recipes, and no source-authored word list, story, game, threshold, or layout entered Homa's skill package.
